title: Finding the Resultant of Two Perpendicular Vectors of Equal Magnitude
notes: **If two vectors of equal magnitude act perpendicular to each other, find the resultant.** Let $|\vec{A}|=|\vec{B}|=a$ and $\theta=90°$. Using $R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2AB\cos\theta}=\sqrt{a^2+a^2+2a^2\cos90°}=\sqrt{2a^2}=a\sqrt2$. Direction: $\tan\alpha=\dfrac{a\sin90°}{a+a\cos90°}=\dfrac{a}{a}=1 \Rightarrow \alpha=45°$ — the resultant bisects the angle between the two equal perpendicular vectors.

**Q. If two equal vectors act perpendicular to each other and their resultant is 1.414 ($\approx\sqrt2$) units, find the magnitude of each vector.** Using $R=a\sqrt2$ from above: $a=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt2}=1$ unit — each vector has magnitude 1 unit.
For two vectors of equal magnitude a at right angles, the parallelogram formula loses the middle term because cos90° = 0. R = sqrt(a^2 + a^2) = a√2.
The direction from either vector satisfies tanα = a/a = 1, so α = 45°. The resultant is exactly between them.
This is the same statement as adding aî and aĵ to get aî + aĵ, whose magnitude is a√2 and whose direction is 45° to each axis.
If a measured resultant of two such vectors is 1.414 units, which is √2 to three decimals, then a√2 = √2 and each vector has magnitude 1.
confusion: 45° is from each vector, so the angle between the vectors is still 90°.
Parallel vectors of magnitude a give 2a, a larger resultant.
keyPoints: The resultant bisects the right angle.
If R is √2, each vector has magnitude 1.

summary: Equal vectors at right angles have resultant a√2 directed halfway between them. The cosine term drops out because cos90° is zero. A resultant of √2 means each vector has magnitude 1.
